subject.title: Execution anti-drift guards: artifact-gated status, escalation timers, and no-idle-after-green

question: Should OpenClaw add a core execution anti-drift enforcement contract for status/artifact progress, durable run guard state, escalation timers, and post-green follow-through?
rationale: Current main has adjacent diagnostics and loop detection, but the requested behavior creates new runtime state, status-delivery rules, telemetry, and likely config/default surfaces that cannot be safely chosen by automation.

options.title: Design bounded core guard contract
options.body: Specify artifact semantics, timer/defaults, durable SQLite ownership, telemetry, and rollout gating before implementation.

options.title: Narrow to existing diagnostics
options.body: Treat the remaining work as smaller follow-ups to stuck-session diagnostics and tool-loop detection without artifact-gated status enforcement.

options.title: Decline core enforcement
options.body: Keep current loop/stall diagnostics only and close the product direction if strict execution-progress enforcement is not desired in core.

recommendation.title: Design bounded core guard contract
recommendation.body: Specify artifact semantics, timer/defaults, durable SQLite ownership, telemetry, and rollout gating before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter is the clearest current-main routing candidate for the adjacent runtime diagnostic and execution guard files in the available history.
